claims.claim: urllib3.Timeout accepts a total parameter that limits the combined connect and read time.
claims.citation: For more granular control you can use a `Timeout` instance which lets you specify separate connect and read timeouts:

claims.claim: urllib3 retries a request that fails with a timeout error by default.
The urllib3.request() function uses a shared PoolManager internally to send requests.
A PoolManager-level timeout applies to every request made through that PoolManager and cannot be overridden.
claims.citation: If you want all requests to be subject to the same timeout, you can specify the timeout at the `PoolManager` level:

claims.claim: A float timeout passed to request() is split evenly between the connect timeout and the read timeout.

claims.claim: Timeouts exist in urllib3 so that requests to slow servers are aborted to protect against denial-of-service attacks.
claims.citation: Timeouts allow you to control how long (in seconds) requests are allowed to run before being aborted.
